Neither was narrated around by any run. | G6 pass: patternOnAfterBestBoard is null yet L1 with guardrail 'the correct move builds/completes YOUR pattern' is the correct route for realized_denied/missed_own, and link.text is board-accurate; every run attributes the fork to the player, honoring the guardrail (G2a). | G7 pass on all runs: annotationRepairs is [] and guardDiagnostics.failures is [] for all 5; every emitted handle wraps a phrase matching its stated role (run 0's 'that fork square' matches the you-double ROLE text even though that role is itself wrong for a 3-cell spec — a render defect, not an answer defect). | Step 0b caveat: assembleGroundedPrompt(buildReasonRenderModel(fv)) run against CURRENT code produces a prompt that DOES offer [zone:you-fork-pivot] / [zone:you-fork-pivot-2] and requires you-fork-pivot-2, and whose you-double role reads 'the fork squares' (plural) — i.e. the render code has drifted since the 08-26 run and the exact gap identified here appears already addressed; the stored render_decision, not the freshly assembled prompt, was used as ground truth for the offered/required set per Step 0.

counterexamples.field_or_glossary: render_decision.zones.aliases (no *-fork-pivot handle offered; requiredSet = you-immediate c3r6 / you-immediate-3 c5r4 / you-immediate-line)
counterexamples.evidence: afterBest 33211531304533201252211005444 wins for you (all columns scr -6, gravity-top majors at c3r6 and c6r5) only because column 5 lands at c5r4 and creates the fork; no handle names that creating square as the move you should have played, and 4/5 runs never identify it.

c3r6 is the top of column 3 — the column actually played (afterPlayed 33211531304533201252211005442 shows X 29 at c3r6). Forcing this handle while never binding c5r4 to 'where you should have played' makes runs 0/1/4 tell the blunderer to take the square they just took, then contradict it with 'by playing column 3 instead'.
